transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-20
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Laura Chen (Redwood AE), Miguel Torres (Redwood SE), Jasmine Park (Redwood Product), Nina Patel (Aurora PM), Samir Rao (Aurora Integration), Priya Menon (Aurora Security), Leo Zhang (Aurora Solutions)

Summary: quick sync on marketplace listing + reference arch + joint solution. focus on staging test, security, and timeline for listing approval.

Topics: marketplace listing requirements, billing/integration, reference architecture and IaC artifacts, security and compliance, go-to-market listing timeline

Action items (discussed): see action_items metadata field above

Transcript body:
[00:00] Laura (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda — marketplace listing, reference arch artifacts, security questions, and then next steps. does that look right to folks?
[00:10] Nina (Aurora): yeah that works. we got a few questions from PM and biz dev about billing integration and the listing metadata.
[00:18] Miguel (Redwood): cool. i'll jump into the reference arch side — i'll show where the dedicated and hosted routing points live and a sample terraform snippet.
[00:26] Samir (Aurora): sounds good. our main ask is to make the installation pattern straightforward for our marketplace — one click deploy or terraform module would be ideal.
[00:35] Laura: perfect. quick callout — we support hosted API, dedicated pools and private VPC installs. for marketplace listing we'll need clear copy about the deployment modes and a recommended default for Aurora customers.
[00:47] Leo (Aurora): do you have a recommended default? most of our customers want predictable latency but not all want a long term reserved capacity.
[00:55] Miguel: recommend Dedicated for higher throughput customers; Hosted API for quick evals. for a marketplace flow we usually show Hosted as the trial path with a button to request Dedicated via our sales form.
[01:05] Nina: ok that helps. what about the billing integration — do you expect us to route billing through Aurora, or can customers use Redwood direct?
[01:14] Laura: both are possible. for marketplace listing standard path is Aurora-billed (we provide a marketplace integration guide). we can also list BYO billing where customer links their Redwood account. we'll include both options in the draft.
[01:27] Priya (Aurora): security — we need to confirm data residency and key management for private deployments. are you offering KMS/HSM integrations?
[01:36] Miguel: yes we have KMS integration for Private and Dedicated; for Hosted we offer customer-managed keys in some regions — though i'll double-check the exact regions, i might be off on the region list in my head.
[01:48] Jasmine (Redwood Product): note: some of the region names can be slightly different in the docs, we should sync that to avoid mismatch on the listing.
[01:56] Samir: also, for the reference architecture we need terraform modules. can you provide tf variables and example helm values so our ops team can replicate?
[02:05] Miguel: absolutely. i'll share a repo with a basic module, a helm values yaml and a sample cloudformation snippet (if you use CF). it's mostly generic: VPC, subnets, SGs, and then the redwood operator helm chart.
[02:19] Nina: what's the timeline for those artifacts?
[02:23] Miguel: i can get a first cut by next week for the diagram, and the tf snippets within 2 weeks — more polished by sept 3.
[02:33] Laura: great. circling back to listing contents — we should include a short blurb about typical latency ranges and cost guidance, maybe a table comparing hosted vs dedicated vs private.
[02:45] Leo: yes please — we get a lot of support questions if customers choose the wrong mode.
[02:50] Priya: on compliance, can you confirm SOC 2 scope and whether you have ISO 27001? our procurement asks both.
[02:58] Laura: we are SOC 2 Type II and certified for ISO 27001 in our control plane; private deployments are in-scope differently, i'll send the standard compliance pack.
[03:08] Priya: okay please send that pack. also audit logs — we want to ensure full request logs are forwarded to our SIEM in private installs.
[03:16] Miguel: yes audit logs can be streamed. couple notes: for hosted we redact some token-level info by default, but for private we can enable full request logging to your ELK/Kafka. i'll document that.
[03:28] Nina: great. on the listing approval process from Aurora side — what artifacts do you need?
[03:33] Laura: typically: product description, icons/screenshots, pricing tiers, support contact, and a short integration guide + security certs. we'll draft the listing copy and share screenshots.
[03:44] Samir: one potential snag — our marketplace requires a validation test where we deploy and run a basic inference workload. can you support us with a test image or script?
[03:54] Miguel: yes i can provide a smoke test harness — basically a small script that pushes sample prompts and validates token throughput and correctness. i'll include a sample dataset and expected outputs.
[04:06] Nina: that is perfect. ok next question: joint solution positioning — we'd like to create a reference arch doc co-branded and a short joint blog announcing the listing. timeline thoughts?
[04:16] Laura: for co-badged reference arch and blog, typical timeline is 4-6 weeks after artifacts are ready. so if tf+diagram are ready by sept 3, a blog in late sept or early oct seems realistic.
[04:26] Leo: we want to align GTM with our marketplace campaign in oct, so that timing works if we hit the artifact deadlines.
[04:33] Priya: security review needs to happen before public listing — can we aim to complete security Q&A by Aug 27?
[04:40] Laura: yes we'll prioritize sending the compliance pack and a short security Q&A doc to Priya by 8/27.
[04:47] Samir: small note, for the smoke test we need sample credentials or a staging API key flow — what do you prefer?
[04:55] Miguel: we'll create time-limited staging API keys via our console; i'll include a short script to rotate them. beware that staging keys are rate-limited.
[05:05] Nina: drifting back to marketplace listing metadata — do you have recommended tags and categories?
[05:11] Jasmine (Redwood): yes tags: "LLM inference", "generative AI", "embeddings", "low-latency". category: "AI infrastructure". we'll include recommended screenshots: console, latency dashboards, and an integration diagram.
[05:22] Leo: can you also provide a short video/gif for the listing — 30 sec demo?
[05:27] Laura: we can do a short gif showing the hosted API chat flow. we'll queue that with marketing and try to get a draft in a week.
[05:36] Priya: question on data retention — hosted customers ask default retention period for logs and data; what do you default to?
[05:42] Miguel: default is 30 days for request logs on hosted, but enterprise customers can change retention for dedicated/private. i'll add this to the doc.
[05:51] Samir: any dependencies we should be aware of for the reference arch e.g. specific k8s versions or helm chart versions?
[05:59] Miguel: recommended k8s 1.24+ and helm 3.9+; we'll put exact tested versions in the repo. also note we support both docker and OCI images but our recommended image tag is the semver pinned release.
[06:12] Nina: outstanding item from procurement — legal needs a simple MSA template for marketplace offers, any gotchas?
[06:19] Laura: for marketplace we typically use a lightweight addendum referencing Aurora marketplace terms; legal can draft and we'll review. the main go/no-go items are data processing terms and indemnity clauses.
[06:30] Priya: please flag encryption-at-rest defaults — we need to ensure private deployments support customer-managed keys.
[06:36] Miguel: confirmed earlier. private + dedicated can integrate with customer KMS; i'll put step-by-step in the security doc.
[06:44] Leo: for go-live checklist, what's the Aurora marketplace acceptance criteria?
[06:49] Nina: typically: installable via our marketplace flow, security checklist signed off, listing copy + assets, and a smoke test passed in staging.
[06:58] Jasmine: ok, so our plan: Laura drafts listing + marketing assets by 8/25; Miguel delivers reference arch diagram + tf by 9/03; Priya gets security pack by 8/27; Samir runs smoke test and reports by 9/07. follow-up demo week of 9/10.
[07:14] Samir: i may need a small window with your SE to debug cluster networking during staging test. can we request a 1 hour SE follow-up?
[07:21] Miguel: yes happy to do a pairing session — i'll block 1 hour after you schedule the staging test.
[07:29] Laura: anything else on the technical side?
[07:32] Leo: one more — do you have any rate-limiting guidance for the marketplace plan? we want to set reasonable defaults so customers don't get surprised.
[07:40] Miguel: for hosted trial plan we throttle to 60 rps per api key and tokens per minute cap; for dedicated it's per-pool and configurable. i'll add recommended quotas to the listing doc.
[07:53] Nina: thanks, that's helpful. procurement will also want to see support SLAs attached to the listing — bronze/silver/gold?
[08:01] Laura: we'll propose standard tiers and the contact flow for escalation. we'll include that in the draft.
[08:08] Priya: last security note — can you provide a sample encryption key rotation procedure? that's usually requested by our infra team.
[08:16] Miguel: yes i'll add a quick runbook for KMS rotation.
[08:19] Laura: ok perfect. let's recap next steps.
[08:24] Nina: recap: listing draft 8/25, security pack 8/27, ref arch + tf 9/03, staging smoke test by 9/07, follow-up demo 9/10.
[08:34] Laura: sounds good. i'll send calendar invites for the follow-up and share a doc with all artifacts.
[08:39] Samir: thanks everyone, we'll try to get the staging environment ready by friday so you can run the smoke test.
[08:45] Miguel: if you run into networking issues ping me on slack and we'll triage.
[08:49] Priya: thanks, looking forward to the compliance docs.
[08:52] Laura: thanks all, talk soon.
[08:56] (call ends)
